gloss: to restrain; to hold back; to dissuade

definitions.gloss: to restrain; to hold back; to stop someone from acting
definitions.explanation: To physically prevent someone from moving or acting, often by pushing or holding them in place.

definitions.gloss: to dissuade; to talk someone out of something
definitions.explanation: To persuade someone not to do something impulsive or risky, convincing them to reconsider their course of action.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}を{押|お}し{留|とど}めた。
{暴|あば}れる{男|おとこ}を{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}が{押|お}し{留|とど}めた。
examples.english: People nearby restrained the man who was acting violently.

examples.japanese: {飛|と}び{出|だ}そうとする{子|こ}どもを{母親|ははおや}が{慌|あわ}てて{押|お}し{留|とど}めた。
examples.english: The mother hurriedly held back the child who was about to run out.

examples.japanese: {退職|たいしょく}しようとする{彼|かれ}を{押|お}し{留|とど}めた。
{友人|ゆうじん}の{無謀|むぼう}な{計画|けいかく}を{押|お}し{留|とど}めた。
examples.english: I talked my friend out of their reckless plan.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}に{転職|てんしょく}を{相談|そうだん}したが、{強|つよ}く{押|お}し{留|とど}められた。
examples.english: I consulted my boss about changing jobs, but was strongly dissuaded.

notes:
A compound verb from {押|お}す (to push) and {留|とど}める (to stop, keep in place). Sense 1 implies physical restraint — literally holding someone back from moving or acting. Sense 2 is more figurative — persuading someone not to do something, often something impulsive or risky.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}を{押|お}し{留|とど}める: to hold someone back
- {怒|いか}りを{押|お}し{留|とど}める: to hold back one's anger
- {強|つよ}く{押|お}し{留|とど}める: to firmly restrain/dissuade

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引|ひ}き{止|と}める: to detain, hold back — emphasizes pulling back; often used for persuading someone to stay
- {制止|せいし}する: to restrain, stop — more formal; often used in official or news contexts
- {止|と}める: to stop — general; lacks the forceful nuance of {押|お}し{留|とど}める
